{{Quote|Since the Death Star, Imperial policy is one of ''caution''. But when the moment is ''right--'' the Empire will ''strike back''!|Ulric Tagge|<ref name="marvel31" />}}
'''Ulric Tagge''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served first as a [[General/Legends|General]] and [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] [[Commander/Legends|commander]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial Military/Legends|Military]], and later as the [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] of the ancient and powerful [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]]. The youngest of four sons, Ulric joined the Imperial service after his brother [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio]], and both brothers became high-ranking [[Officer/Legends|officers]]. But Cassio's [[Death/Legends|death]] in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] made Ulric the focal point of his eldest brother, Baron [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge's]] plots to gain the favor of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Orman's used his family connections to get Ulric placed in charge of the Imperial [[Yavin blockade|blockade]] of the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]], and in turn Ulric provided military support to several of his brothers' schemes, most notably an effort to destroy a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] fleet in the [[Feswe Corridor]] with a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] called the [[Omega Frost/Legends|Omega Frost]]. The Omega Frost endeavor turned into a [[Battle of the Corridor|disaster]] after the interference of Rebel [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and both Orman and brother [[Silas Tagge/Legends|Silas Tagge]] were seemingly killed, leaving Ulric as the new Baron Tagge. Afterwards, Ulric retired from Imperial service to focus on his new duties with the Tagges' business holdings.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Welcome, General. Or should I say Baron? I understand the family title has recently fallen to you. My congratulations on that&mdash;and on your narrow escape from the Rebels. Even if it did cost the Empire a cruiser."<br />"Is this why you called me from duty, Vader... to taunt me?"<br />"I called you because it suits my purposes, my insolent, ambitious young friend!|Darth Vader and Ulric Tagge|<ref name="marvel35">[[Star Wars (1977) 35|''Star Wars'' (1977) 35]]</ref>}}
[[File:Tagges.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Ulric Tagge with his sister Domina.]]
A [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Tepasi/Legends|Tepasi]], Ulric Tagge was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] a younger son of the rich and venerable [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]], the owners of the megacorporation known as the [[Tagge Company/Legends|Tagge Company]] and one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] wealthiest and most prestigious families. Ulric grew up in the shadow of his three elder brothers: [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman]], groomed from birth to be the family's next [[Baron/Legends|Baron]]; [[Silas Tagge/Legends|Silas]], a natural-born [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]]; and [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio]], a careful strategist destined to go into military service. Awed and intimidated by his brothers, Ulric spent much of his youth with his sister [[Domina Tagge/Legends|Domina]], with whom he felt most comfortable.<ref name="geonosis" /> Ulric and Domina were eventually separated when Domina was sent to [[Monastery/Legends|Monastery]] in order to join the [[Order of the Sacred Circle]], a religious organization the Tagges hoped would keep Domina free from [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] and corporate intrigues&mdash;<ref name="marvel36">[[Star Wars (1977) 36|''Star Wars'' (1977) 36]]</ref> afterward, Ulric followed Cassio into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial Military/Legends|Military]], earning a reputation as an effective, if unimaginative [[Officer/Legends|officer]].<ref name="geonosis" /> Tagge was promoted to [[General/Legends|General]] by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], personally commanding a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] called the ''[[Peacehawk]]'', and promoting an ambitious young man named [[Zertik Strom/Legends|Zertik Strom]] to [[Executive officer/Legends|First Officer]] after Strom distinguished himself by crushing a rebellion among the [[Poporov merchants]] of [[Armstiss]]. Strom served Tagge brilliantly in that position, going on to become one of the youngest officers ever to command his own [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of patrol ships.<ref name="vegas">{{SW|url=news/viva-space-vegas-the-history-of-the-marvelous-wheel-part-2|series=Viva Space Vegas! The History of the Marvelous Wheel|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

Ulric's rise up the Imperial ranks was mirrored by his brother Cassio, who himself became a high-ranking general and, by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the head of [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] operations aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]].<ref name="dstc">[[Death Star Technical Companion (Second Edition)|''Death Star Technical Companion'', Second Edition]]</ref> However, Cassio was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] destroyed the station during their stunning victory in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="dbtagge">{{DB|character|generaltagge|Tagge, General}}</ref> leaving Ulric as the focal point for Orman's plots to gain the favor of the [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor]]. Orman used his family connections and [[Politics/Legends|political]] maneuverings to secure Ulric a post as a [[Major General]] and command of a Tagge fleet that [[Yavin blockade|blockaded]] the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]] after the battle on behalf of the Imperials.<ref name="geonosis" /> Ulric directed the blockade with assistance from Orman and Silas, who operated a device known as [[Achtnak Turbine Station]] in order to effectively disguise [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] runs on the Rebels' [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] base.<ref name="marvel25">[[Star Wars (1977) 25|''Star Wars'' (1977) 25]]</ref> However, Orman and Silas were nearly killed when Rebel [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] destroyed the station, sending the Tagges back to the drawing board.<ref name="marvel26">[[Star Wars (1977) 26|''Star Wars'' (1977) 26]]</ref>

Before long, Orman and Silas returned to Ulric with another plot, much to the General's chagrin. This time around, the elder Tagge brothers had developed a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] called the [[Omega Frost/Legends|Omega Frost]], which they hoped could freeze an entire Rebel fleet. Although Ulric was skeptical about Orman's desire to upstage the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], he again pledged to lend his brother the support of his battle group, pending successful tests of the device on the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="marvel31" /> When the experiments on Tatooine proved successful, the Tagge brothers met again above the planet [[Feriae Junction/Legends|Feriae Junction]], where Orman transferred the Omega Frost's conductor towers onto Ulric's [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. The Tagges set up the device within the nearby [[Feswe Corridor]], a major Rebel supply route, and planned to use the Omega Frost to obliterate a fleet of Rebel [[DP20 gunship/Legends|gunships]].<ref name="marvel33" /> Ulric's part was to stay nearby to provide any needed military support, as well as provide a record of his brothers' success to the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. However, Skywalker managed to destroy one of the conductor towers, foiling their plot&mdash;moments later, Ulric watched as the Rebel [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] destroyed his brothers' [[Mining Explorer]], seemingly killing both.<ref name="marvel34">[[Star Wars (1977) 34|''Star Wars'' (1977) 34]]</ref> Ulric himself managed to escape the Rebel assault, and indicated on his official report that the [[Battle of the Corridor|defeat]] was merely the result of a standard blockade action.<ref name="marvel35" />

[[File:VaderUlric.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Darth Vader Force chokes Ulric Tagge.]]
Believed by the galaxy to be the last living Tagge brother, Ulric suddenly found himself the new Baron Tagge. He soon received another unwelcome surprise in a visit from Darth Vader, who wanted the truth about the defeat at the Corridor. Tagge spilled the beans after experiencing a Vader [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Choke|choke]], after which Vader revealed a secret that shocked Tagge to his core: Orman and Silas still lived, having somehow survived the destruction of their ship. Vader held Orman and Silas in [[life support capsule]]s aboard his Star Destroyer, and offered to keep their survival a secret&mdash;allowing Ulric's claim to the title of Baron to remain unchallenged&mdash;in exchange for his unquestioning loyalty and obedience. Tagge accepted the offer<ref name="marvel35" /> and traveled to Monastery to meet with Domina, who had since become the leader of the Order of the Sacred Circle. There, Tagge informed her that Orman and Silas were dead, and that her best chance to get revenge on Skywalker was to join forces with Vader.<ref name="marvel36" /> After visiting Domina on Monastery, Ulric retired from military service to focus on his new responsibilities as the steward of the Tagges' business holdings.<ref name="geonosis" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Not another plan, Orman! The last was nearly as great a fiasco as the Death Star!|Ulric Tagge, to his brother Orman|<ref name="marvel31" />}}
Unlike the flashy and ambitious Orman, Ulric Tagge was content not rocking the boat&mdash;growing up in the shadow of his three elder brothers, Tagge simply wanted to be seen as a competent military officer unburdened by excessive imagination or aspiration. Of his siblings, Ulric was only particularly close with his sister Domina, and solely felt real happiness when in her company. But the death of his brother Cassio at the Battle of Yavin flung Ulric into Orman's plots, and the youngest Tagge brother dutifully followed.<ref name="geonosis" /> However, while Ulric played his part in Orman's schemes, he did not always do so eagerly, as he was often dubious of their success and wary of Orman's animus towards Darth Vader.<ref name="marvel31" /> Ulric was proud of his new station upon ascending to the title of Baron Tagge,<ref name="marvel36" /> and jumped at the opportunity to keep his surviving brothers hidden away in Vader's custody, attempting to justify his decision as concern for his sister Domina.<ref name="marvel35" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ulric Tagge first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 31|''Star Wars'' (1977) 31]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and released in [[1979]].<ref name="marvel31" /> A "General Tagge" previously appears in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], and Goodwin originally intended the two characters to be one and the same, with Ulric having escaped the destruction of the Death Star at the end of the film.<ref name="insider">{{InsiderCite|96|The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military}}</ref> However, the [[2004]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] supplement ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' established the movie general's first name as Cassio,<ref name="geonosis">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> while the original [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] conclusively established Ulric and Cassio Tagge as brothers.<ref name="db">{{DB|character|generaltagge|Tagge, General}}</ref> During Tagge's comic appearances, he was illustrated by [[Carmine Infantino]].<ref name="marvel31" />
